result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.compose()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compose this graph with another graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15735-L15793){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.compose(other) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Compose](/assets/graphs/compose.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same G and H as for union, except that the shared fourth node is labeled D in G (accent) and D′ in H (teal). Compose merges nodes by id and keeps all four edges like union, but H wins the clash, so the result shows D′." width="100%"} Similar to union, but the other graph's node attributes/labels take precedence over this graph's. Useful when you want to merge updates from another graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph to compose with (its attributes take precedence). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new composed graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graphs have different directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Compose is a right-biased `union()`: the same edge set is produced, but wherever both graphs carry a value for the same node or edge, the *other* graph's value wins. This makes it the natural primitive for applying updates or overlays to a base graph without losing edges that were only in the base. Both operands must share the same directedness. ## Examples {.doc-examples} `compose()` behaves like `union()`, but lets the second graph's attributes overwrite the first's -- useful for applying an update to a base graph: ::: {#34c427b8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Original graph g1 = ec.Graph(directed=False) g1.add_node(label="Alice") g1.add_node(label="Bob") g1.add_edge("Alice", "Bob") # Update: same node ID as "Alice", but a new label g2 = ec.Graph(directed=False) g2.add_node(label="Robert") result = g1.compose(g2) result.get_node(1).label ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 'Robert' ``` ::: :::
